text:
liam: ran the ensemble bakeoff (AWQ + GPTQ) on the legal-qa suite this morning. overall avg accuracy is fine but the formatting tasks show a 3.2% hallucination spike vs FP8 baseline :confused:

marta: ugh. which subset exactly? formatting = date/number/markdown outputs?

liam: yes, mostly 'legal-formatting' subset (citations, numbered lists, statute refs). config: AWQ-int8 (group_size=128, per-channel), GPTQ-int8 baseline, FP8 reference. temp=0.2, beam=1.

sophia: were these batched evals or single-request? batching can hide kv-cache / alignment issues.

liam: batch size 8 for throughput sim. i re-ran batch=1 and seed=42 — hallucination down ~1.1% but not fully recovered. seed seems to matter.

jay: could be token-shift due to quant rounding accumulating in KV cache. we saw similar with small group_size. try group_size=64 and per-tensor to compare.

liam: good call. also saw weird diffs where numbered lists drop item numbers and insert extra text. pasted a quick diff of outputs: 
```
FP8: "(1) The statute 12.4 states...
"
AWQ: "The statute 12.4 states... Additionally, the court found..."
```

eva: logs show occasional repeated tokens in hidden states around step 14 for the problematic prompts. i dumped activations for a few seeds. attaching minimal excerpt below: 
```
# activ dump (token idx, mean activation)
seed=7: idx14: 0.0034 -> 0.0091
seed=42: idx14: 0.0035 -> 0.0036
seed=99: idx14: 0.0033 -> 0.0102
```

marta: can someone paste the exact eval command used? i'll spin up a small repro.

liam: command i used: 
```bash
python eval.py --model awq-int8-ensemble --subset legal-formatting --seed 7 --batch-size 8 --temp 0.2 --out results/awq_seed7.json
```

alex: couple of experiments to prioritize: (1) deterministic single-thread seed runs, (2) group_size sweep [32,64,128], (3) per-tensor vs per-channel quant, (4) re-run with kv-cache flushing between requests to rule it out. i'll queue them in the CI matrix.

deploy-bot: queued job #4421: quant-sensitivity/ensemble/seed-sweep (links: https://ci/internal/4421) :white_check_mark:

sophia: also try eval with logits-clipping (small epsilon) — sometimes quantized logits cause overconfidence that manifests as hallucination.

jay: and capture top-k token probs for the first 20 tokens to see if the distribution is shifting early.

liam: thanks. i'll collect the group_size sweep + kv-flush runs and post a short table. if we still see seed dependence after kv flush, we probably need to revisit quant calibration. :eyes:
